title.title: The Correspondence of the Yarnall family

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of the Yarnall family is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: Hearing that thee was under some difficulty about keeping thy colt, and I apprehending thee would not willingly sell it, I spoke to John Macksfield about keeping of it, who says he will keep it for thee at a reasonable rate till thee can see a way to dispose of it otherwise. I intend to be at Philadelphia next seventh day, come week being the last seventh day in this month and if I can get a passage I shall come to see you. I thought, if some of your neighbors were down at market I should be willing ride up with them. We are all in as good health as usual at present.
div.closer: So I conclude and remain thy affectionate Mother– Elizabeth Evans Evesham 3rd mo 20th 1793
